title: Building AI Agents with Real ROI in the Enterprise SDLC: Bruno (Booking.com) & Beyang (Sourcegraph)
talk_summary: Booking.com and Sourcegraph describe building SDLC agents (GraphQL schema navigation, legacy code migration, tailored PR review) and the organizational/metric scaffolding around them. The most transferable mechanisms are rule-file-driven review agents optimized for precision, retrieval-over-huge-context instead of stuffing context windows, and divide-and-conquer decomposition for large migrations.

takeaways.technique: Rule-file-driven review agent with precision bias
takeaways.what_they_do: Define review rules in a simple flat-file format; the agent loads rules, applies only the relevant ones to the files changed in a PR, and posts selective comments tuned to those rules, explicitly optimizing precision over recall.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the agent will go and consume those rules apply the relevant ones to the specific files that are modified ... very selectively post up comments

takeaways.technique: Retrieval + tree-walk over oversized schemas instead of stuffing context
takeaways.what_they_do: For a >1M-token GraphQL schema that fits no context window, they search for relevant nodes, agentically reason about which are relevant, then walk up the tree to pull parent nodes before generating.
Before automating a legacy migration, they spent effort sizing the problem and locating call sites, then split the codebase into small conquerable units so the agent works on bounded pieces.

takeaways.technique: Per-task model selection by observed expertise
takeaways.what_they_do: They removed single-LLM limits and let developers pick among multiple LLMs because different models performed better on legacy excavation vs. greenfield feature work.

takeaways.technique: Replace vanity 'hours saved' with measurable KPIs
takeaways.what_they_do: They discarded self-reported 'I saved' metrics as statistically weak and defined four KPIs (lead time for change, quality, codebase health, modernization) measurable within a year, tracking daily-user cohorts vs. non-users.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I saved wasn't the most statistically relevant metric ... we Define new kpis which I'll go deeper into
takeaways.numbers: 30%+ faster for daily users; 30% more MRs shipped

takeaways.technique: Prompt library + education as the adoption lever
takeaways.what_they_do: They built a shared prompt library and ran workshops/hackathons, finding that developers who abandoned the tool did so from lack of prompting/context knowledge, not tool failure.
takeaways.evidence_quote: pure lack of knowledge uh folks didn't know how to work llms out they didn't know how to pass the right prompt in the right context
